records.source_meaning: Angelo calls out to someone as a low-ranking underling. Preserve the patronizing insult without assigning Camille a canonical crew rank or duty.
records.fresh_source_gloss: Angelo calls out to someone as a low-ranking underling. Preserve the patronizing insult without assigning Camille a canonical crew rank or duty.
records.whole_exchange_context: Angelo rudely calls Camille an underling and dismisses the value of an introduction through him. This is Angelo's belittling address,not proof of Camille's actual shipboard rank. Lil defends Camille bycalling Angelo okama,a dated derogatory gendered label for an effeminate/gay man. Angelo angrily denies it andcalls her a brat. Preserve the insult/denial exchange as their speech,not a narrator assertion about Angelo's sexuality or gender identity,anddo not invent women's clothing or a drag performance. Both characters are rude;Camille lateracknowledges that Lil was rude too. The insult should remain recognizable and the offended response should follow naturally without adding unrelated abuse. Optional Fernando comments on Lil's childish conduct. Camille defuses the argument,introduces himself andLil with FI/FA,andidentifies her as admiral. Angelo apologizes after learning her role. Lil objects to Camille apologizing for her;Angelo agrees with her andadmits he teases cute boys/guys. Keep that attraction/teasing cue without inventing a romance or fixed identity label. Camille awkwardly accepts the apology,thenstops Angelo leaving andoffers him a place as a navigator/crew companion. Lil andoptional Fernando object because Camille was insulted;Camille sees good in Angelo andvalues varied travel companions. Fernando admits Camille's generosity is a virtue butcannot read Angelo;Lil relents in exasperation. Camille welcomes Angelo before even asking his name;Angelo notices Camille has effectively persuaded Lil,apologizes again andintroduces himself as Angelo Puccini. Camille leads him toward the ship whileLil protests being left behind. Angelo corrects his familiar little-lady address to Admiral;Lil sweetly threatens to make him work hard. No invented kinship or earned recruitment outcome is claimed by prose. The same full block continues intoAngelo's Mediterranean-versus-Africa trade advice,withoptional Julio commentary. Existing developed routes look attractive,butmajor powers have already developed anddominate the Mediterranean,raising contract/investment costs andlimiting opportunities. Angelo recommends Africa as having development potential andunusual goods for Europe trade;the expected profits remain his argument,not a verified universal rule or a promise of a specific amount. He modestly attributes it to sailors' talk;Julio endorses the market-share logic andexplains thatmore cargo capacity doesnot ensure large transactions when European shares are difficult to acquire. Lil excitedly decides to head for Africa andmake money this time. Retain this progression from insult to apology,unexpected welcome,playful authority andpractical travel motivation. Source macro counts are {'FI': 5, 'FA': 1, 'FO': 0};branch/resource/pause/recruitment effects are separate native obligations.

records.whole_exchange_context: Angelo rudely calls Camille an underling and dismisses the value of an introduction through him. This is Angelo's belittling address,not proof of Camille's actual shipboard rank. Lil defends Camille bycalling Angelo okama,a dated derogatory gendered label for an effeminate/gay man. Angelo angrily denies it andcalls her a brat. Preserve the insult/denial exchange as their speech,not a narrator assertion about Angelo's sexuality or gender identity,anddo not invent women's clothing or a drag performance. Both characters are rude;Camille lateracknowledges that Lil was rude too. The insult should remain recognizable and the offended response should follow naturally without adding unrelated abuse. Optional Fernando comments on Lil's childish conduct. Camille defuses the argument,introduces himself andLil with FI/FA,andidentifies her as admiral. Angelo apologizes after learning her role. Lil objects to Camille apologizing for her;Angelo agrees with her andadmits he teases cute boys/guys. Keep that attraction/teasing cue without inventing a romance or fixed identity label. Camille awkwardly accepts the apology,thenstops Angelo leaving andoffers him a place as a navigator/crew companion. Lil andoptional Fernando object because Camille was insulted;Camille sees good in Angelo andvalues varied travel companions. Fernando admits Camille's generosity is a virtue butcannot read Angelo;Lil relents in exasperation. Camille welcomes Angelo before even asking his name;Angelo notices Camille has effectively persuaded Lil,apologizes again andintroduces himself as Angelo Puccini. Camille leads him toward the ship whileLil protests being left behind. Angelo corrects his familiar little-lady address to Admiral;Lil sweetly threatens to make him work hard. No invented kinship or earned recruitment outcome is claimed by prose. The same full block continues intoAngelo's Mediterranean-versus-Africa trade advice,withoptional Julio commentary. Existing developed routes look attractive,butmajor powers have already developed anddominate the Mediterranean,raising contract/investment costs andlimiting opportunities. Angelo recommends Africa as having development potential andunusual goods for Europe trade;the expected profits remain his argument,not a verified universal rule or a promise of a specific amount. He modestly attributes it to sailors' talk;Julio endorses the market-share logic andexplains thatmore cargo capacity doesnot ensure large transactions when European shares are difficult to acquire. Lil excitedly decides to head for Africa andmake money this time. Retain this progression from insult to apology,unexpected welcome,playful authority andpractical travel motivation. records.whole_exchange_context: Angelo rudely calls Camille an underling and dismisses the value of an introduction through him. This is Angelo's belittling address,not proof of Camille's actual shipboard rank. Lil defends Camille bycalling Angelo okama,a dated derogatory gendered label for an effeminate/gay man. Angelo angrily denies it andcalls her a brat. Preserve the insult/denial exchange as their speech,not a narrator assertion about Angelo's sexuality or gender identity,anddo not invent women's clothing or a drag performance. Both characters are rude;Camille lateracknowledges that Lil was rude too. The insult should remain recognizable and the offended response should follow naturally without adding unrelated abuse. Optional Fernando comments on Lil's childish conduct. Camille defuses the argument,introduces himself andLil with FI/FA,andidentifies her as admiral. Angelo apologizes after learning her role. Lil objects to Camille apologizing for her;Angelo agrees with her andadmits he teases cute boys/guys. Keep that attraction/teasing cue without inventing a romance or fixed identity label. Camille awkwardly accepts the apology,thenstops Angelo leaving andoffers him a place as a navigator/crew companion. Lil andoptional Fernando object because Camille was insulted;Camille sees good in Angelo andvalues varied travel companions. Fernando admits Camille's generosity is a virtue butcannot read Angelo;Lil relents in exasperation. Camille welcomes Angelo before even asking his name;Angelo notices Camille has effectively persuaded Lil,apologizes again andintroduces himself as Angelo Puccini. Camille leads him toward the ship whileLil protests being left behind. Angelo corrects his familiar little-lady address to Admiral;Lil sweetly threatens to make him work hard. No invented kinship or earned recruitment outcome is claimed by prose. The same full block continues intoAngelo's Mediterranean-versus-Africa trade advice,withoptional Julio commentary. Existing developed routes look attractive,butmajor powers have already developed anddominate the Mediterranean,raising contract/investment costs andlimiting opportunities. Angelo recommends Africa as having development potential andunusual goods for Europe trade;the expected profits remain his argument,not a verified universal rule or a promise of a specific amount. He modestly attributes it to sailors' talk;Julio endorses the market-share logic andexplains thatmore cargo capacity doesnot ensure large transactions when European shares are difficult to acquire. Lil excitedly decides to head for Africa andmake money this time. Retain this progression from insult to apology,unexpected welcome,playful authority andpractical travel motivation.
